title: British European Airways 706

agencies.name: Accidents Investigation Branch
agencies.report_title: Civil Aircraft Accident Report 15/72 - British European Airways Vanguard G-APEC

summary: British European Airways Flight 706, a Vickers Vanguard, crashed near Aarsele, Belgium on October 2, 1971 while climbing through flight level 190. The rear pressure bulkhead failed due to undetected metal fatigue corrosion, causing rapid depressurization of the tail section and separation of both horizontal tailplanes. The aircraft entered an uncontrollable dive from which recovery was impossible. All 63 occupants perished.
probable_cause: The accident was caused by the rupture of the rear pressure bulkhead, which led to the separation of both tailplanes in flight and caused the aircraft to dive into the ground. The rupture occurred due to undetected metal fatigue corrosion at the rear pressure bulkhead. (p. 36)

factors.evidence: Inspection techniques used for detecting corrosion at station 1223 were inadequate; radiographic technique used was ineffective at detecting corrosion due to difficulty interpreting photographic plates from complex structure (p. 34)

Severe corrosion present at joint between fuselage skin and rear pressure bulkhead for unknown period prior to accident; progressive crack in bulkhead grew through at least fourteen successive pressurization cycles (p. 34)
Rear pressure bulkhead ruptured in cruising flight at FL 190 when corrosion-initiated crack exceeded critical crack length (p. 36)

Rapid inflation of tailcone and empennages from bulkhead rupture imposed high differential pressure causing upper tailplane skin panels to detach from main structure; both horizontal tailplanes and elevators separated in flight (p. 33)
Loss of aerodynamic download from horizontal tail surfaces caused aircraft to pitch rapidly nose-down; entered steep dive from which it was not possible to recover (p. 33)

events.text: Flight 706 took off from runway 28L at London Heathrow with 55 passengers and 8 crew members; climbed through 14,200 feet at Dover VOR (p. 3)
Aircraft handed over to Brussels Air Traffic Control at mid-channel on airway Green One; satisfactory two-way communications established; aircraft climbing toward flight level 190 (p. 3)
Aircraft reported passing over Wulpen VOR with aircraft level at FL 190; flight proceeding normally with no indication of abnormality (p. 3)
Aircraft in level flight at FL 190 with flight proceeding normally; flight recorder ceased to function indicating start of structural failure sequence (p. 33)

Rear pressure bulkhead ruptured due to corrosion-initiated crack exceeding critical length; rapid inflation of tailcone and empennages imposed high differential pressure across tailplane skins (p. 36)
Crew transmitted we are going down, 706, we're going down immediately followed by MAYDAY call repeated several times (p. 3)
Fragmented and garbled transmissions continuing with phrases we're going down vertically and out of control (p. 3)

Upper tailplane skin panels became detached from main structure as differential pressure imposed high loads; existing aerodynamic loads caused both horizontal tailplanes to become detached in flight (p. 33)
Loss of aerodynamic download from separated tailplanes caused aircraft to pitch rapidly nose-down (p. 33)

Aircraft in steep dive with longitudinal attitude between 20° and 30° over vertical, rotating slowly in clockwise direction about longitudinal axis at high forward speed; transmissions ceased abruptly at ground impact (p. 3)
Aircraft struck open farmland near Aarsele Belgium in steep dive; completely destroyed by ground impact and subsequent fire; all 63 occupants killed (p. 3)

cvr.speaker: PF
cvr.text: we are going down, 706, we're going down

safety_changes: Introduction of improved inspection techniques for detecting corrosion in rear pressure bulkhead
Modification to Vanguard aircraft to improve inspection access to station 1223 area
Increased frequency of inspection of bonded joints in pressure bulkheads
Recommendation to install modification L 40 on Vanguard aircraft to strengthen tailplane attachments
